words.enDefinition: Support such as money, goods, or services provided by a sponsor for a particular event.

examples.en: The ceramics club sought event sponsorship to cover the cost of printing its exhibition programme.
examples.zh: 陶艺社寻求「活动赞助」，用于支付展览手册的印刷费用。

examples.en: Event sponsorship helped the student organisers run a second workshop after the first one filled.
examples.zh: 首场工作坊满员后，「活动赞助」帮学生组织者加开了一场。

words.enDefinition: Sponsorship provided as goods or services, such as equipment, materials, or use of a space.

examples.en: A local printer offered in-kind sponsorship by producing programmes for the student film festival.
examples.zh: 本地一家印刷店提供「非现金赞助」，为学生电影节印制手册。

examples.en: The club listed the loan of display boards as in-kind sponsorship for its spring exhibition.
examples.zh: 社团把借用展板列为春季展览的「非现金赞助」。

words.zhGloss: 实物或服务形式的资助
words.enDefinition: A specific contribution made in goods, services, or facilities instead of money.
acceptedZhAnswers: 实物或服务形式的资助

examples.en: We recorded the donated picture frames as an in-kind contribution to our student art show.
examples.zh: 我们把获赠的相框记为学生艺术展的「实物资助」。

examples.en: The event summary listed printing as an in-kind contribution from the shop across the road.
examples.zh: 活动小结把马路对面商店提供的印刷服务列为一笔「非现金资助」。

words.enDefinition: A person or organisation that donates goods or services in place of money.

examples.en: The neighbourhood café was an in-kind donor for the club's first student art show.
examples.zh: 街坊咖啡馆是社团首场学生艺术展的「非现金捐赠方」。

examples.en: We contacted the in-kind donor to confirm how many blank sketchbooks would be available.
examples.zh: 我们联系了「非现金捐赠方」，确认能提供多少本空白素描本。

words.enDefinition: A person or organisation that supports an activity with money.

examples.en: A cash sponsor offered to cover the printing costs for our student photography exhibition.
examples.zh: 一位「现金赞助方」提出承担学生摄影展的印刷费用。

examples.en: The organiser thanked the cash sponsor after explaining how the money was used for the event.
examples.zh: 组织者说明这笔款项在活动中的用途后，感谢了「现金赞助方」。

words.enDefinition: Features the sponsor is offered in return for support, such as recognition on event materials.

examples.en: The proposal described sponsor benefits including a logo on the cover of our exhibition programme.
examples.zh: 提案列出了「赞助方可获得的回报」，包括在展览手册封面放置赞助方标识。

examples.en: We agreed on sponsor benefits before the café committed to providing drinks for our workshop.
examples.zh: 咖啡馆承诺为工作坊提供饮品之前，我们先谈定了「赞助方可获得的回报」。

words.enDefinition: Public acknowledgement of a sponsor's contribution to an event or project.

examples.en: The designer set aside the last page for sponsor recognition in our student film programme.
examples.zh: 设计师留出学生电影节手册的最后一页，用于「公开鸣谢赞助方」。

examples.en: We chose a short announcement for sponsor recognition at the start of the exhibition.
examples.zh: 我们决定在展览开场时简短广播，「公开鸣谢赞助方」。

collocations: review sponsor recognition in the programme

words.zhGloss: 赞助方标识的位置安排
words.enDefinition: The planned location of a sponsor's logo on a sign, printed item, or other material.
acceptedZhAnswers: 赞助方标识的位置安排

examples.en: The designer checked sponsor logo placement before sending the poster draft to the student organisers.
examples.zh: 设计师把海报草稿发给学生组织者之前，确认了「赞助方标识的位置安排」。

examples.en: The draft agreement included a diagram showing sponsor logo placement on the welcome banner.
examples.zh: 协议草案附了一张图，展示欢迎横幅上「赞助方标识的位置安排」。

words.enDefinition: A line of text naming the person or organisation that sponsored an event or project.

examples.en: Please add the sponsor credit line below the title before the programmes go to print.
examples.zh: 手册送印之前，请在标题下方加上「赞助方署名行」。

examples.en: I checked the sponsor credit line against the bakery's official name on its website.
examples.zh: 我核对了「赞助方署名行」，看看和面包店官网上的正式名称是否一致。

words.zhGloss: 以呈献名义署名的赞助方
words.enDefinition: A sponsor prominently credited as presenting an event in some of its publicity.
acceptedZhAnswers: 以呈献名义署名的赞助方
以呈献方名义署名的赞助商

examples.en: The presenting sponsor was credited directly under the festival title on the programme cover.
examples.zh: 活动手册把「以呈献名义署名的赞助方」列在节庆名称正下方。

examples.en: We asked the presenting sponsor to approve how its name appeared beside the exhibition title.
examples.zh: 我们请「以呈献名义署名的赞助方」确认其名称在展览标题旁怎么展示。

words.enDefinition: The sponsor with the principal supporting role among several sponsors for an event or project.

examples.en: The craft shop became our lead sponsor after offering materials for all four student workshops.
examples.zh: 这家手工艺品店提出为四场学生工作坊提供材料，成为我们的「主要赞助方」。

examples.en: The lead sponsor was invited to meet the student organisers before the showcase opened.
examples.zh: 展演开场前，「主要赞助方」受邀和学生组织者见面。

words.enDefinition: One of two or more people or organisations supporting the same event as sponsors.

examples.en: The student newspaper joined as a co-sponsor and helped publicise the exhibition across campus.
examples.zh: 学生报以「联合赞助方」的身份加入，帮助在校园里宣传展览。

examples.en: We listed each co-sponsor separately so visitors could see who contributed to the event.
examples.zh: 我们分别列出了每个「联合赞助方」，让访客知道哪些单位为活动做了贡献。

words.enDefinition: A level of sponsorship associated with an expected contribution and a set of benefits.

examples.en: The brochure described a sponsorship tier for small shops that could donate materials or equipment.
examples.zh: 宣传册介绍了一个面向小商店的「赞助级别」，这些商店可以捐赠材料或设备。

examples.en: Each sponsorship tier had a different offer for how partners would be named on signs.
examples.zh: 每个「赞助级别」对如何在标牌上为合作方署名有不同安排。

words.enDefinition: A bundle of contribution options or benefits offered to a potential sponsor.

examples.en: Our club prepared a sponsorship package for local shops interested in supporting the student market.
examples.zh: 社团为有意支持学生市集的本地商店准备了一份「赞助方案」。

examples.en: The bakery reviewed the sponsorship package and asked whether its name would appear on signs.
examples.zh: 面包店看了「赞助方案」，问标牌上会不会出现店名。

words.enDefinition: A document or presentation proposing how a sponsor could support a project and what it would receive.

examples.en: Our sponsorship proposal explained who would visit the exhibition and what the printer could contribute.
examples.zh: 我们的「赞助提案」说明了展览的观众是谁，以及印刷店可以提供哪些支持。

examples.en: The café manager asked to see the sponsorship proposal before discussing the event with us.
examples.zh: 咖啡馆经理希望先看「赞助提案」，再和我们讨论活动。

words.enDefinition: The person named to handle enquiries and details about an event's sponsorship.

examples.en: The poster listed a sponsorship contact for businesses interested in lending equipment to the organisers.
examples.zh: 海报列出了「赞助对接人」，方便有兴趣借出设备的商家联系组织者。

examples.en: I emailed the sponsorship contact to confirm when the books would arrive at the venue.
examples.zh: 我给「赞助对接人」发了邮件，确认书什么时候送到场地。

words.enDefinition: Supplies or raw materials given freely to support a project or activity.

examples.en: The student studio used donated materials to make signs for the community repair event.
examples.zh: 学生工作室用「捐赠的材料」制作社区维修活动的指示牌。

examples.en: We sorted the donated materials before deciding what to use for the workshop demonstrations.
examples.zh: 我们先整理了「捐赠的材料」，再决定工作坊演示用哪些。

collocations: credit the source of donated materials

words.enDefinition: Tools or equipment given to a group for it to keep and use.

examples.en: The student workshop received donated equipment when a print shop cleared out its old studio.
examples.zh: 一家印刷店清理旧工作室时，给了学生工场一批「获赠设备」。

examples.en: The organiser checked the donated equipment against the list before adding it to the shared studio.
examples.zh: 组织者先把「获赠设备」与清单核对，再把设备放进共用工作室。

words.enDefinition: Professional work or practical help provided free of charge as a contribution.

examples.en: The event team listed donated services such as photography and basic editing in its final report.
examples.zh: 活动团队在最终报告中列出了摄影和简单剪辑等「获赠的服务」。

examples.en: We budgeted for printing separately because the donated services only covered the design work.
examples.zh: 我们单独给印刷留了预算，因为「获赠的服务」只包括设计。

words.enDefinition: Used on event materials to credit a person or organisation that helped fund or provide something.

examples.en: The programme described the exhibition as supported by the local print shop and two student clubs.
examples.zh: 手册写明，展览「由本地印刷店和两家学生社团提供支持」。

examples.en: A sign at reception said the film night was supported by several local businesses.
examples.zh: 接待处的标牌写着，电影之夜「由几家本地商户提供支持」。

words.enDefinition: Used to identify who provided particular goods or materials for an activity or job.

examples.en: The display stands were supplied by the art studio next door for the weekend.
examples.zh: 这些展架在周末「由隔壁艺术工作室供应」。

examples.en: The handout listed which materials were supplied by the campus store for the demonstration.
examples.zh: 讲义列出了演示材料里有哪些「由校园商店供应」。

collocations: refreshments supplied by a local shop

words.enDefinition: A slide naming the people or organisations whose help is being recognised.

examples.en: The students added an acknowledgement slide naming the print shop that supplied their posters.
examples.zh: 学生们加了一张「致谢幻灯片」，写上为他们提供海报的印刷店名称。

examples.en: The acknowledgement slide appeared while the organiser thanked the club's partners at the end.
examples.zh: 活动尾声，组织者向社团合作方道谢时，屏幕上显示了「致谢幻灯片」。

words.enDefinition: Signs that display the names or logos of an event's sponsors.

examples.en: The venue manager checked the sponsor signage before we opened the student market to visitors.
examples.zh: 学生市集对访客开放前，场地方检查了「展示赞助方的标牌」。

examples.en: We agreed to put sponsor signage near the welcome table where visitors could see it.
examples.zh: 我们同意把「展示赞助方的标牌」放在迎宾台附近，让访客能看见。

collocations: set aside space for sponsor signage

words.enDefinition: A message or record confirming that a sponsor has agreed to provide the proposed support.

examples.en: We received sponsorship confirmation just before the catalogue went to the student printer that afternoon.
examples.zh: 那天下午，目录送去学生运营的印刷店前，我们收到了「赞助确认」。

examples.en: The sponsorship confirmation listed the equipment the business had agreed to lend for the exhibition.
examples.zh: 「赞助确认」列出了商家同意借给展览的设备。

words.enDefinition: A promise made by a sponsor to provide specified support for an activity.

examples.en: The sponsor commitment covered printing the programmes for both days of the student film festival.
examples.zh: 「赞助方承诺」包括为学生电影节两天的活动印制手册。

examples.en: Our treasurer recorded the sponsor commitment after the shop told us how many signs it could print.
examples.zh: 商店告诉我们可以印多少块标牌后，财务负责人记录了「赞助方承诺」。

collocations: confirm a sponsor commitment in writing

words.enDefinition: An agreement to continue sponsorship beyond the original event, period, or arrangement.

examples.en: The club discussed sponsorship renewal after the bakery helped with two successful student events.
examples.zh: 面包店支持的两场学生活动都办得很成功，社团之后讨论了「续订赞助安排」。

examples.en: The business asked about sponsorship renewal before agreeing to supply materials for the next semester.
examples.zh: 商家先问了「续订赞助安排」的事，再同意为下学期提供材料。

words.enDefinition: A person or organisation that may agree to sponsor a project but has not yet committed.

examples.en: We showed a prospective sponsor photographs of last year's exhibition before describing our new plans.
examples.zh: 介绍新计划前，我们给「潜在赞助方」看了去年展览的照片。

examples.en: The studio invited a prospective sponsor to visit while students were preparing the display boards.
examples.zh: 学生们准备展板时，工作室邀请一位「潜在赞助方」来参观。

collocations: send materials to a prospective sponsor

words.enDefinition: A message inviting a person or organisation to support a particular project as a sponsor.

examples.en: The club sent a sponsorship invitation to the company that supplied its old display stands.
examples.zh: 社团给以前提供展架的公司发了份「赞助邀请」。

examples.en: The café responded to our sponsorship invitation and asked which event needed the drinks.
examples.zh: 咖啡馆回复了我们的「赞助邀请」，问哪场活动需要饮品。

words.enDefinition: A notice clarifying that naming or recognising an organisation does not mean recommending it or its products.

examples.en: The programme said No endorsement implied beside the list of businesses that supplied the materials.
examples.zh: 手册在材料供应商名单旁注明「不代表支持或认可」。

examples.en: Our group discussed what No endorsement implied meant before approving the acknowledgement page for printing.
examples.zh: 批准印制致谢页前，我们小组讨论了「不代表支持或认可」是什么意思。

collocations: a note saying no endorsement implied
read the no endorsement implied note

words.enDefinition: A table set aside at an event for a sponsor's representatives, materials, or display.

examples.en: The organiser reserved a sponsor table near reception so the bakery could display its samples.
examples.zh: 组织者在接待处附近预留了「赞助方展示桌」，方便面包店摆放样品。

examples.en: I checked the sponsor table had enough space for the leaflets and photo display.
examples.zh: 我确认了「赞助方展示桌」有足够空间摆传单和照片展品。

words.enDefinition: An organisation working with another group to plan or carry out an activity.

examples.en: Each collaborating organization sent someone to the planning meeting for our student design fair.
examples.zh: 每个「参与协作的机构」都派人参加了学生设计市集的筹备会。

examples.en: We asked the collaborating organization to bring photographs for the shared display about the project.
examples.zh: 我们请「参与协作的机构」带些照片，用于共同展示项目。

words.enDefinition: The person responsible for coordinating work between the groups in a partnership.

examples.en: Our partnership lead checked which group was bringing equipment for each afternoon workshop session.
examples.zh: 「合作负责人」核对了每天下午的工作坊分别由哪个小组带设备。

examples.en: The student centre named a partnership lead to coordinate our work with the print studio.
examples.zh: 学生中心指定了一名「合作负责人」，协调我们与印刷工场的工作。

words.enDefinition: The way two people or organisations relate to each other when they work together.

examples.en: The student studio built a working relationship with the local theatre by making signs together.
examples.zh: 学生工作室通过和当地剧院一起制作标牌，建立了「工作合作关系」。

examples.en: Clear handover notes helped us keep a good working relationship with the people using the space next.
examples.zh: 清楚的交接记录让我们和下一批使用场地的人保持了良好的「工作合作关系」。

words.enDefinition: A short document outlining what a joint project is for and what each group will do.

examples.en: The collaboration brief explained which team would design the signs and who would check them.
examples.zh: 「合作任务简报」说明了哪个团队设计标牌，以及由谁检查。

examples.en: We gave the print shop a collaboration brief before discussing how much it could contribute.
examples.zh: 讨论印刷店可以提供多少支持之前，我们先给了他们一份「合作任务简报」。

words.enDefinition: A document or presentation suggesting how two groups could work together and what each would contribute.

examples.en: Our partnership proposal suggested that the student group manage the exhibition and the studio lend equipment.
examples.zh: 我们的「合作提案」建议由学生小组管理展览，工作室出借设备。

examples.en: The gallery asked us to explain our roles more clearly in the partnership proposal.
examples.zh: 画廊请我们在「合作提案」中更清楚地说明各自的角色。

words.enDefinition: To divide the duty of looking after an activity or task with another person or group.

examples.en: The two clubs agreed to share responsibility for arranging the display boards before the exhibition.
examples.zh: 两家社团同意「共同负责」在展览前布置展板。

examples.en: Our studio and the student centre share responsibility for checking returns after each weekend event.
examples.zh: 我们的工作室和学生中心「共同负责」核对每次周末活动后的归还物品。

collocations: agree to share responsibility for the equipment

words.enDefinition: Used to name the people or groups that did the work of organising an activity together.

examples.en: The poster said the market was jointly organized by the studio and the student union.
examples.zh: 海报写着，市集「由工作室和学生会联合组织」。

examples.en: The exhibition was jointly organized by the film society and a studio near the station.
examples.zh: 展览「由电影社和车站附近的一家工作室联合组织」。

collocations: an event jointly organized by students

words.enDefinition: A person or group that shares the work of organising an event with another.

examples.en: The print studio joined as a co-organizer and helped arrange the workshops for new members.
examples.zh: 印刷工场以「联合组织者」身份加入，帮忙为新成员安排工作坊。

examples.en: Each co-organizer checked the final programme before we sent it to the other partners.
examples.zh: 发给其他合作方之前，每个「联合组织者」都检查了最终版活动手册。

collocations: name a co-organizer in the programme

words.enDefinition: The principal person or group coordinating the organisation of an event or activity.

examples.en: The lead organizer confirmed who would open the venue and where speakers should leave their bags.
examples.zh: 「牵头组织者」确认了谁来开场馆门，以及演讲者可以把包放在哪里。

examples.en: Our club acted as lead organizer for the exhibition with support from two local studios.
examples.zh: 当地两家工作室提供支持，我们社团担任展览的「牵头组织者」。

collocations: the lead organizer for an event

words.enDefinition: A partner that provides a location or takes responsibility for welcoming participants and running an activity.

examples.en: The hosting partner showed us where to put the display tables before the market opened.
examples.zh: 市集开放前，「协作承办方」领我们去看了展示桌的位置。

examples.en: Our hosting partner arranged a small room for visiting artists to prepare their materials.
examples.zh: 「协作承办方」安排了一个小房间，给来访的艺术家准备材料用。

words.enDefinition: A group or unit within a university or college that works with you on a project.

examples.en: The library became our campus partner for an exhibition about how students use shared spaces.
examples.zh: 图书馆成为我们的「校内合作方」，一起举办展览，介绍学生如何使用共用空间。

examples.en: We asked our campus partner which rooms could accommodate both demonstrations on the same day.
examples.zh: 我们问「校内合作方」有哪些房间能在同一天容纳两场演示。

words.enDefinition: A business in the surrounding area that works with a group on a shared project.

examples.en: The club invited a local business partner to show students how it prints small runs.
examples.zh: 社团邀请「本地商家合作方」向学生展示怎样小批量印刷。

examples.en: Our local business partner lent two display stands for the exhibition at the student centre.
examples.zh: 「本地商家合作方」借了两个展架给学生中心的展览用。

collocations: work with a local business partner

words.enDefinition: A partner that helps make, assemble, or produce the materials or finished work for a project.

examples.en: Our production partner cut the display boards after we agreed on the finished dimensions.
examples.zh: 我们商定成品尺寸后，「制作合作方」裁切了展板。

examples.en: We chose a production partner that could print the large photographs without trimming their borders.
examples.zh: 我们选了一家「制作合作方」，能印大照片而且不会裁掉边缘。

words.enDefinition: To make a room, building, or other space available for an organised event.

examples.en: The gallery agreed to provide the venue while the student club arranged speakers and volunteers.
examples.zh: 画廊同意「提供活动场地」，学生社团负责邀请讲者和组织志愿者。

examples.en: A local workshop offered to provide the venue for the first open day in spring.
examples.zh: 当地的一家工作室愿意为春季第一个开放日「提供活动场地」。

collocations: provide the venue for a workshop

words.enDefinition: To pay separate shares of the costs of booking and using an event space.

examples.en: The two student groups agreed to split the venue costs before advertising the weekend market.
examples.zh: 宣传周末市集前，两个学生小组同意「分摊场地费用」。

examples.en: We asked how to split the venue costs when one partner needed an extra room.
examples.zh: 有一家合作方需要额外一间房，我们问该怎样「分摊场地费用」。

collocations: agree to split the venue costs
decide how to split the venue costs

words.enDefinition: A workspace used by different artists, makers, or groups for their own work or joint projects.

examples.en: The student design group used a shared studio to finish its signs for the market.
examples.zh: 学生设计小组在「共用工作室」里做完了市集标牌。

examples.en: We keep unfinished display panels in the shared studio while both groups prepare their exhibitions.
examples.zh: 两个小组各自准备展览时，我们把没完成的展板放在「共用工作室」。

collocations: book space in a shared studio

words.enDefinition: A table or surface used by more than one person or group to build or prepare things.

examples.en: I left the shared workbench clear so the next group could lay out its prints.
examples.zh: 我把「共用工作台」清空，让下一组可以摊开印刷品。

examples.en: We booked a shared workbench for assembling folders and checking display labels on Thursday.
examples.zh: 我们预订了「共用工作台」，周四用来装资料夹和检查展品标签。

words.enDefinition: Permission or an arrangement allowing someone to enter and use a studio.

examples.en: We arranged studio access for both design teams while they worked on the exhibition signs.
examples.zh: 两支设计团队做展览标牌时，我们给他们安排了「工作室使用权限」。

examples.en: The coordinator checked studio access before asking our group to collect the printed programmes.
examples.zh: 协调员先确认了「工作室使用权限」，再请我们小组去领印好的手册。

words.enDefinition: An arrangement giving members access to a studio and any facilities included with membership.

examples.en: Our studio membership included weekly access to a table large enough for the display maps.
examples.zh: 我们的「工作室会员资格」包含每周使用一张大桌子的权限，那桌子够铺开展示地图。

examples.en: I asked about studio membership because our group needed somewhere to prepare posters each month.
examples.zh: 我们小组每月都需要地方做海报，所以我问了「工作室会员资格」的事。

words.enDefinition: To reserve a period during which you can work in a studio.

examples.en: We had to book studio time for cutting the panels before the display was assembled.
examples.zh: 展品组装之前我们得「预约工作室使用时段」来裁切面板。

examples.en: Our group decided to book studio time when both designers could check the artwork together.
examples.zh: 我们组决定「预约工作室使用时段」，选两位设计员都能一起核对图稿的时候。

collocations: book studio time for a group

words.enDefinition: A booking to use particular equipment at an agreed date or time.

examples.en: I made an equipment reservation for the large trimmer we needed to finish the posters.
examples.zh: 我做了「设备预约」，订了完成海报所需的大裁纸机。

examples.en: The studio coordinator confirmed our equipment reservation before telling us when to collect the kit.
examples.zh: 工作室协调员确认了我们的「设备预约」，再告诉我们什么时候去领器材。

words.enDefinition: An introductory session explaining what equipment is available and how it is used in a workspace.

examples.en: The studio offered an equipment orientation for student teams preparing to use the shared workspace.
examples.zh: 工作室向即将使用共用空间的学生团队提供了「设备使用介绍」。

examples.en: Our equipment orientation included a tour of the tools the display teams could reserve later.
examples.zh: 「设备使用介绍」包括带我们看一遍展示团队之后可以预约的工具。

collocations: offer equipment orientation to new users

words.enDefinition: A place set aside for the supplies or equipment of one group or project.

examples.en: The workshop offered dedicated storage for our large boards between the two exhibition dates.
examples.zh: 两场展览之间，工场为我们的大展板提供了「专用存放空间」。

examples.en: Our team requested dedicated storage so unfinished signs would stay separate from the other group's tools.
examples.zh: 我们团队申请「专用存放空间」，好把没做完的标牌和另一组的工具分开放。

words.enDefinition: A place where several people or groups keep their supplies or equipment.

examples.en: Each group labelled its boxes before putting them in the shared storage area for the fair.
examples.zh: 各组给自己的箱子贴上标签，才放进市集的「共用存放区」。

examples.en: We checked the shared storage area before ordering another set of stands for the exhibition.
examples.zh: 给展览另订一套展架前，我们先查了「共用存放区」。

collocations: label items in a shared storage area

words.enDefinition: A service or collection that lends tools for people to use and return.

examples.en: The campus tool library lent our workshop clamps for assembling the display boards on Friday.
examples.zh: 周五我们要组装展板，校园「工具借用处」借了些夹具给我们工场。

examples.en: We used the tool library before deciding which equipment our group actually needed to buy.
examples.zh: 我们先用「工具借用处」的服务，再决定小组到底需要购置哪些设备。

words.enDefinition: A record showing who used equipment and when or how it was used.

examples.en: The studio checked its equipment use log to see which team used the projector last.
examples.zh: 工作室查了「设备使用记录」，看看最后用了投影仪的是哪个团队。

examples.en: I added our workshop time to the equipment use log before leaving the shared studio.
examples.zh: 离开共用工作室前，我把我们使用设备的时间填进了「设备使用记录」。

collocations: fill in the equipment use log

words.enDefinition: The state of loaned goods or equipment at the time they are brought back.

examples.en: The studio recorded the condition on return after our group brought back the display stands.
examples.zh: 我们小组还回展架后，工作室记录了它们「归还时的状况」。

examples.en: Both partners checked the condition on return before putting the borrowed projector back into storage.
examples.zh: 借来的投影仪放回储藏室之前，双方核对了它「归还时的状况」。

words.enDefinition: The hours during which people with permission can use a studio.

examples.en: We checked studio access hours before arranging to work on the signs after our classes.
examples.zh: 安排下课后做标牌之前，我们先查了「工作室可使用时段」。

examples.en: The notice listed studio access hours separately for the exhibition teams and regular members.
examples.zh: 通知分别列出了展览团队与普通会员的「工作室可使用时段」。

words.enDefinition: An agreement about how two or more users will use the same workspace.

examples.en: Our space-sharing arrangement gave each team its own table while keeping the shelves available to everyone.
examples.zh: 按「场地共用安排」，每组有自己的桌子，架子则所有人都能用。

examples.en: The gallery reviewed its space-sharing arrangement after a third student group asked to use the studio.
examples.zh: 第三个学生小组申请使用工作室后，画廊重新看了「场地共用安排」。

words.enDefinition: Use of the space by one group alone for an agreed period.

examples.en: We booked exclusive use of the space while two student groups recorded a joint performance.
examples.zh: 两个学生小组录制联演节目时，我们订了「单独使用该场地」的时段。

examples.en: The event organiser asked about exclusive use of the space during the launch on Friday.
examples.zh: 活动组织者问，周五发布会期间能否「单独使用该场地」。

collocations: book exclusive use of the space
ask about exclusive use of the space
pay for exclusive use of the space

words.enDefinition: The quantity or value of materials available to a person or group as part of an arrangement.

examples.en: Our materials allowance covered paper for the workshop and cardboard for a single display board.
examples.zh: 我们的「材料使用额度」包括工作坊用纸和制作一块展板的纸板。

examples.en: We split the materials allowance between two groups after checking how many posters each needed.
examples.zh: 我们先确认每组需要多少海报，再在两组之间分配「材料使用额度」。

words.enDefinition: To bring borrowed tools or other equipment back by the agreed time.

examples.en: We promised to return equipment on time so the next student team could start its session.
examples.zh: 我们答应「按时归还设备」，好让下一组学生开始活动。

examples.en: The reminders helped both teams return equipment on time after the afternoon workshop ended.
examples.zh: 下午工作坊结束后，提醒让两个团队记得「按时归还设备」。

collocations: agree to return equipment on time
remember to return equipment on time
help teams return equipment on time

words.enDefinition: To bring or supply the materials needed for your work yourself.

examples.en: The workshop notice said to provide your own materials for making signs at the studio.
examples.zh: 工作坊通知写明，在工作室做标牌需要「自行准备材料」。

examples.en: The organiser said to provide your own materials if you wanted to make a second display.
examples.zh: 组织者说，如果想做第二件展品，就要「自行准备材料」。

collocations: need to provide your own materials
agree to provide your own materials
ask whether to provide your own materials

words.enDefinition: A document setting out what service a provider will perform and what the client and provider agree to do.

examples.en: The student design team reviewed the services agreement before taking on the exhibition signage job.
examples.zh: 学生设计团队接下展览标牌的活之前，看了「服务协议」。

examples.en: Our services agreement described the setup work the studio would carry out on Friday.
examples.zh: 我们的「服务协议」说明了工作室周五要做哪些布置工作。

collocations: include something in the services agreement

words.enDefinition: A document describing the work to be done, including its scope, deliverables, and expectations.

examples.en: The organiser wrote a statement of work for the group making signs for the showcase.
examples.zh: 组织者为给展演制作标牌的小组写了份「工作说明书」。

examples.en: We checked the statement of work to see whether the photographer would also edit the images.
examples.zh: 我们查阅「工作说明书」，看看摄影师是否也负责修图。

words.enDefinition: The tasks, services, or results that a team or supplier is expected to provide.

examples.en: The scope of work covered designing the signs and preparing the files for printing.
examples.zh: 「工作范围」包括设计标牌和准备印刷文件。

examples.en: We checked whether transporting the stands fell within the scope of work for the workshop.
examples.zh: 我们确认了运输展架是否属于工场的「工作范围」。

words.enDefinition: A short description of what needs to be done for a particular assignment or piece of work.

examples.en: The studio gave us a job brief for making new labels for the shared shelves.
examples.zh: 工作室给了我们一份「工作任务简要说明」，要求为共用架子做新标签。

examples.en: The job brief said who would check the finished folders before the student fair opened.
examples.zh: 「工作任务简要说明」写明了学生市集开放之前由谁检查做好的资料夹。

words.enDefinition: A document explaining what a design should achieve and listing its key requirements and constraints.

examples.en: The design brief asked for a poster that could be read from across the entrance hall.
examples.zh: 「设计任务书」要求海报从入口大厅对面也能看清。

examples.en: We asked the gallery to check the design brief before our team drafted the new signs.
examples.zh: 我们团队开始画新标牌草稿之前，请画廊核对了「设计任务书」。

words.enDefinition: A document listing detailed requirements or characteristics such as sizes, materials, or formats.

examples.en: The specification sheet listed the exact size of the boards needed for the outdoor display.
examples.zh: 「规格表」列出了户外展品所需展板的确切尺寸。

examples.en: The studio asked for a specification sheet before selecting the right cover stock for our catalogue.
examples.zh: 在给目录选合适的封面用纸之前，工作室请我们提供一份「规格表」。

words.enDefinition: Materials the client provides for someone else to use in carrying out agreed work.

examples.en: The printer checked the client-supplied materials before agreeing to use them for the exhibition signs.
examples.zh: 印刷店先核查了「委托方提供的材料」，再同意用于制作展览标牌。

examples.en: The brief listed photographs and paper samples among the client-supplied materials for the job.
examples.zh: 任务书把照片和纸样列为这项工作中「委托方提供的材料」。

collocations: draw up a list of client-supplied materials

words.enDefinition: The client's formal or informal agreement to something before work continues or is accepted.

examples.en: We waited for client approval before adding the new sponsor's name to both banner designs.
examples.zh: 我们先等「委托方确认」，再把新赞助方的名称加到两份横幅设计里。

examples.en: The designer asked for client approval before making the same change on both programme covers.
examples.zh: 设计员先请「委托方确认」，再在两份手册封面作同样的修改。

words.enDefinition: Tasks the client is expected to carry out under a service arrangement.

examples.en: The document listed client responsibilities such as supplying photographs and checking the spelling of names.
examples.zh: 文件列出了「委托方职责」，比如提供照片和核对姓名拼写。

examples.en: We discussed client responsibilities at the first meeting so both teams knew who supplied the artwork.
examples.zh: 初次开会时，我们讨论了「委托方职责」，让双方知道由谁提供图稿。

words.enDefinition: Tasks the supplier is expected to perform as part of an arrangement to provide goods or services.

examples.en: The table of supplier responsibilities included wrapping the printed panels before we picked them up.
examples.zh: 「供应方职责」表中包括在我们取件前包好印制的展板。

examples.en: We checked supplier responsibilities to see who would provide the stands for the finished signs.
examples.zh: 我们核对了「供应方职责」，看看由谁为做好的标牌提供支架。

words.enDefinition: One designated person or team through whom all messages or requests about an arrangement are handled.

examples.en: The printer named a single point of contact for both our design questions and artwork approvals.
examples.zh: 印刷店指定了「统一对接人」，处理我们的设计问题和图稿确认。

examples.en: Our coordinator was the single point of contact so updates did not get lost between groups.
examples.zh: 为避免进展信息在小组间漏传，我们的协调员担任「统一对接人」。

collocations: designate a single point of contact
act as a single point of contact
provide a single point of contact

words.enDefinition: A note stating which revisions or how many rounds of changes are included in the service.

examples.en: We checked the line marked “Revisions included” before sending our draft poster to the designer.
examples.zh: 我们先看了标为「包含的修改次数」的一栏，再把海报草稿发给设计员。

examples.en: The quote showed “Revisions included” under the description of the student society's design package.
examples.zh: 学生社团的设计方案说明下，报价单列出了「包含的修改次数」。

collocations: check revisions included in the quote
list revisions included in the package

words.enDefinition: The maximum number of revisions or rounds of changes allowed for a piece of work.

examples.en: The designer suggested a revision limit so the poster would be ready before the exhibition.
examples.zh: 为了在展览前做好海报，设计员建议定一个「修改次数上限」。

examples.en: We reached the revision limit after sending separate comments on the colours and the layout.
examples.zh: 颜色和版式的意见我们分开提，之后就达到了「修改次数上限」。

words.enDefinition: One cycle of collecting comments and making a set of changes based on them.

examples.en: We combined everyone's comments for one round of revisions before checking the poster again on Friday.
examples.zh: 我们汇总所有人的意见，进行「一轮修改」，周五再核对海报。

examples.en: After the first round of revisions, the team agreed to keep the original cover image.
examples.zh: 「第一轮修改」结束后，团队同意保留原来的封面图片。

words.enDefinition: The expected amount of time needed to complete a job once the necessary materials are available.

examples.en: The student printer gave us an estimated turnaround after seeing the size of the display boards.
examples.zh: 学生运营的印刷店看到展板大小后，告诉了我们「预计完成所需时间」。

examples.en: The estimated turnaround changed because two of the files needed larger images before printing.
examples.zh: 其中两个文件要换成尺寸更大的图片才能印刷，所以「预计完成所需时间」变了。

words.enDefinition: A service carried out more quickly than the provider's ordinary process.

examples.en: We asked about expedited service when the organiser needed the new signs by Friday morning.
examples.zh: 组织者周五上午就要用新标牌，我们问了「加急服务」的事。

examples.en: The studio could offer expedited service for the labels after another small job was postponed.
examples.zh: 另一项小工作推迟后，工作室能为这批标签提供「加急服务」。

collocations: ask whether expedited service is available

words.enDefinition: The date the people involved have agreed and confirmed for a service to take place.

examples.en: The confirmed service date mattered because the photographer needed someone to open the gallery early.
examples.zh: 摄影师需要有人提早打开画廊，所以「已确认的服务日期」很重要。

examples.en: We checked the confirmed service date before telling volunteers when to move the display tables.
examples.zh: 我们先核对了「已确认的服务日期」，再通知志愿者什么时候搬展示桌。

collocations: ask for the confirmed service date
write down the confirmed service date

words.enDefinition: Putting furniture or equipment in place before an event and taking it down when it is over.

examples.en: The service quote included setup and breakdown for the two display areas near the entrance.
examples.zh: 服务报价包括入口附近两个展示区的「布置和撤场」。

examples.en: Our team planned for setup and breakdown while the venue confirmed when the doors would open.
examples.zh: 场地方确认开放时间时，我们团队安排「布置和撤场」。

collocations: allow time for setup and breakdown

words.enDefinition: A note indicating that putting equipment or materials in place is part of the service.

examples.en: We chose the option with setup included because volunteers could not get in before noon.
examples.zh: 因为志愿者中午前进不去，我们选了「含现场布置」的方案。

examples.en: The quote said “Setup included” next to the line for the rented display stands.
examples.zh: 报价单在租用展架这一项旁标明「含现场布置」。

collocations: ask whether setup included is an option

words.enDefinition: Not included in the tasks or services originally agreed for a project.

examples.en: Transporting the display boards was outside the scope of the work agreed with the studio.
examples.zh: 运送展板「不在与工作室约定的工作范围内」。

examples.en: The organiser asked whether redesigning the invitations would be outside the scope of the printing job.
examples.zh: 组织者问，重新设计请柬是否「不在印刷工作的约定范围内」。

words.enDefinition: To ask someone doing a job to also carry out a task beyond the original plan.

examples.en: We needed to request additional work when the gallery asked for more labels on opening day.
examples.zh: 画廊开幕当天又需要一些标签，我们得「提出额外工作请求」。

examples.en: The organiser explained how to request additional work after approving the original list of tasks.
examples.zh: 组织者解释了批准原任务清单后，如何「提出额外工作请求」。

collocations: request additional work from the supplier

words.enDefinition: A change to what tasks or results are included in the work originally agreed.

examples.en: Adding a second display board counted as a scope change in our agreement with the studio.
examples.zh: 按照我们与工作室的协议，多做一块展板算作「工作范围变更」。

examples.en: The team agreed on the scope change before moving the printing date to the following week.
examples.zh: 团队先商定了「工作范围变更」，再把印刷日期挪到下一周。

words.enDefinition: A request to alter a task, requirement, or other detail in work that has been planned.

examples.en: The organiser sent a change request asking us to use the new logo on the signs.
examples.zh: 组织者发来一份「变更申请」，请我们在标牌上用新的标识。

examples.en: The printer reviewed our change request and said the new paper size was available.
examples.zh: 印刷店看了我们的「变更申请」，说可以用新的纸张尺寸。

words.enDefinition: To give permission for tasks beyond the original plan to go ahead.

examples.en: The coordinator could authorize extra work after checking that the budget would cover two new signs.
examples.zh: 协调员确认预算够做两块新标牌后，可以「准许开展额外工作」。

examples.en: Our student group asked who could authorize extra work once the original quote had been accepted.
examples.zh: 接受原报价后，我们学生小组问谁能「准许开展额外工作」。

collocations: ask someone to authorize extra work
be able to authorize extra work

words.enDefinition: A document recording an approved adjustment to previously agreed work and any related details.

examples.en: The change order recorded the extra panel and set a new date for the finished signs.
examples.zh: 「已批准的变更单」记下了新增面板，并为完成整套标牌定了新日期。

examples.en: The printer received a change order before replacing the original cover paper with thicker stock.
examples.zh: 印刷店收到「已批准的变更单」后，把原封面纸换成了较厚的纸。

collocations: check the revised schedule on a change order

words.enDefinition: The gradual addition of extra tasks or requirements beyond what a project originally included.

examples.en: The student studio noticed scope creep when the poster job began to include new window signs.
examples.zh: 做海报的工作开始包括制作新橱窗标牌时，学生工作室注意到「工作范围逐渐扩大」。

examples.en: We recorded new tasks separately to see whether scope creep was affecting the exhibition deadline.
examples.zh: 我们把新任务分开记录，好判断「工作范围逐渐扩大」是否影响了展览的最后期限。

words.enDefinition: A timetable of when parts of an agreed service will be carried out.

examples.en: The service schedule showed when the studio would bring the stands and collect them after closing.
examples.zh: 「服务安排表」写明了工作室何时送来展架，以及闭馆后何时取回。

examples.en: Our coordinator updated the service schedule after the gallery moved the opening to Saturday.
examples.zh: 画廊把开幕改到周六后，我们的协调员更新了「服务安排表」。

words.enDefinition: The latest time by which a person must confirm or approve something for work to continue as planned.

examples.en: We set an approval deadline so the printer would have enough time for both programme covers.
examples.zh: 我们定了「确认批准的最后期限」，好让印刷店有足够时间做两份手册的封面。

examples.en: The designer asked whether the approval deadline applied to the poster or the banner too.
examples.zh: 设计员问「确认批准的最后期限」是只针对海报，还是也适用于横幅。

words.enDefinition: Restricted to the particular event being discussed rather than other events or later uses.

examples.en: The designer said use of the artwork was limited to this event when we asked about reprinting.
examples.zh: 我们问能否重印时，设计员说图稿「仅限用于本次活动」。

examples.en: The offer of free equipment was limited to this event because the university needed it back.
examples.zh: 因为学校需要收回设备，免费出借的器材「仅限用于本次活动」。

collocations: use is limited to this event
access is limited to this event
a licence limited to this event

words.enDefinition: Given an individual price estimate outside the original package or quote.

examples.en: Additional banners were separately quoted after the studio reviewed our new list of display areas.
examples.zh: 工作室看了新展示区名单后，为新增横幅「单独报价」。

examples.en: The email explained that mounting the prints would be separately quoted once we chose a size.
examples.zh: 邮件说明，等我们选好尺寸，会对装裱印刷品「单独报价」。

collocations: check which items are separately quoted

words.enDefinition: An important planned point that marks completion of a stage of a project.

examples.en: We reached a project milestone when both clubs approved the final layouts for the exhibition.
examples.zh: 两个社团都认可展览的最终版式时，我们达到了一个「项目里程碑」。

examples.en: Our studio marked the first sample as a project milestone on the exhibition preparation calendar.
examples.zh: 我们工作室在展览筹备日历上把首件样品标为一个「项目里程碑」。

words.enDefinition: A document, sample, or other output provided before the whole project is complete.

examples.en: The marked floor plan was an interim deliverable before the student studio built the panels.
examples.zh: 学生工作室做展板前，带标记的平面图是一项「阶段交付物」。

examples.en: We reviewed an interim deliverable so the organisers could confirm the size of the signs.
examples.zh: 我们先审查了一项「阶段交付物」，让组织者确认标牌的大小。

words.enDefinition: The date by which a particular agreed item or piece of work needs to be provided.

examples.en: The deliverable due date was Friday because the programmes went to print the following Monday.
examples.zh: 「交付截止日」是周五，因为手册下周一就要送印。

examples.en: Our coordinator checked the deliverable due date before arranging the club's final review of the artwork.
examples.zh: 我们的协调员先确认了「交付截止日」，再安排社团最终审核图稿。

words.enDefinition: The file type, physical form, or other format in which agreed work will be provided.

examples.en: We agreed on the delivery format before the photographer edited the images for our catalogue.
examples.zh: 摄影师为我们的目录修图之前，我们先商定了「交付格式」。

examples.en: The brief described the delivery format for both the digital posters and the printed handouts.
examples.zh: 任务书说明了电子海报和纸质讲义各自的「交付格式」。

words.enDefinition: Agreement that a sample meets expectations so work on the rest can continue.

examples.en: We waited for sample approval before asking the workshop to cut the remaining display panels.
examples.zh: 我们等「样品确认」后，才请工场裁切剩下的展板。

examples.en: The coordinator recorded sample approval once both partners had checked the shape and colour.
examples.zh: 两家合作方核对形状和颜色后，协调员记录了「样品确认」的结果。

words.enDefinition: A sample made before the main run to show how the finished goods are expected to look or work.

examples.en: The student team checked a pre-production sample before ordering enough canvas bags for the fair.
examples.zh: 学生团队在订购市集所需数量的帆布袋之前，检查了「生产前样品」。

examples.en: The workshop brought a pre-production sample so we could test whether the stand fit our table.
examples.zh: 工场带来一个「生产前样品」，好让我们试试展架能不能放到桌上。

words.enDefinition: A preview of printed or designed work that has been checked and accepted for production.

examples.en: The printer kept the approved proof with the job notes for our student society booklet.
examples.zh: 印刷店把「已确认的校样」和学生社团小册子的制作记录放在一起。

examples.en: I compared the finished handout with the approved proof while we counted the boxes at collection.
examples.zh: 取件点数时，我把做好的讲义和「已确认的校样」作了比较。

words.enDefinition: A preview used to check the appearance and content of a piece before printing it.

examples.en: I found a typo in the print proof and sent it back to the designer.
examples.zh: 我在「印刷校样」里发现一个错字，就把它发回给设计员。

examples.en: The print proof showed how the map would look at the actual size of the handout.
examples.zh: 「印刷校样」显示了地图按讲义的实际尺寸印出来会是什么样。

words.enDefinition: The finished version of the graphic design prepared for use or production.

examples.en: The gallery received the final artwork for the banner two days before the exhibition opened.
examples.zh: 展览开幕前两天，画廊收到了横幅的「最终图稿」。

examples.en: We checked the final artwork to make sure the sponsor's name matched the lettering on the poster.
examples.zh: 我们核对了「最终图稿」，确保赞助方名称和海报上的写法一致。

words.enDefinition: A file prepared in the format and quality needed for printing without further adjustments.

examples.en: The photographer sent a print-ready file for the display board after checking the printer's requirements.
examples.zh: 摄影师确认印刷店的要求后，发来了展板的「可直接印刷的文件」。

examples.en: Our student studio could not start the job until we had received a print-ready file.
examples.zh: 直到收到「可直接印刷的文件」，我们的学生工作室才能开工。

words.enDefinition: Permission to begin printing something once its content and layout have been checked.

examples.en: The organiser gave approval to print after correcting a speaker's name on the programme cover.
examples.zh: 组织者更正了手册封面上一位讲者的姓名后，「同意付印」。

examples.en: The student studio waited for approval to print after replacing the old venue name in the artwork.
examples.zh: 学生工作室把图稿上的旧场地名换掉后，等对方「同意付印」。

words.enDefinition: An agreed length of time in which someone examines work before responding or accepting it.

examples.en: The review period gave both student groups time to check the changes before approving the designs.
examples.zh: 「审查期」给了两个学生小组时间，让大家在批准设计前检查修改内容。

examples.en: We asked whether the review period ended before the studio closed for the summer break.
examples.zh: 我们问「审查期」是否在工作室放暑假前结束。

words.enDefinition: Requirements that a finished item or piece of work needs to meet before the client accepts it.

examples.en: Our acceptance criteria said the signs needed to be legible from the entrance to the hall.
examples.zh: 我们的「验收标准」要求，从大厅入口能看清这些标牌。

examples.en: The studio checked the finished display boards against the acceptance criteria in the task brief.
examples.zh: 工场按任务书里的「验收标准」检查了做好的展板。

words.enDefinition: To confirm that the item or service provided is satisfactory under the agreed requirements.

examples.en: We could accept the work once both groups confirmed the finished banner matched the proof.
examples.zh: 双方确认做好的横幅与校样一致后，我们就可以「确认验收」。

examples.en: The coordinator was ready to accept the work after checking the names on every printed folder.
examples.zh: 协调员核对了每个印制资料夹上的姓名后，准备「确认验收」。

collocations: decide whether to accept the work
be ready to accept the work
accept the work after checking it

words.enDefinition: A review to check whether submitted work meets the requirements for acceptance.

examples.en: The gallery arranged an acceptance review so both partners could inspect the signs in daylight.
examples.zh: 画廊安排了一次「验收审查」，让两家合作方能在白天检查标牌。

examples.en: The organiser invited two people from the student group to take part in the acceptance review.
examples.zh: 组织者请学生小组的两个人参与「验收审查」。

words.enDefinition: A list of the items, documents, or other results a team is expected to provide.

examples.en: We agreed on a deliverables list before asking the student studio for a design quote.
examples.zh: 请学生工作室为设计报价前，我们商定了「交付物清单」。

examples.en: The gallery checked the deliverables list to see whether social media graphics were included too.
examples.zh: 画廊查了「交付物清单」，看看是否也包含社交媒体用图。

words.enDefinition: To hand over parts of agreed work at separate times as successive stages are completed.

examples.en: The printer agreed to deliver in stages so we could check the programmes before the banners.
examples.zh: 印刷店同意「分阶段交付」，这样我们能先验手册，再验横幅。

examples.en: We decided to deliver in stages because the floor plans were ready before the display labels.
examples.zh: 因为平面图比展品标签先准备好，我们决定「分阶段交付」。

words.enDefinition: A bundle of final files, notes, or other materials passed to the person taking over a project.

examples.en: The handover package included the approved artwork and the addresses of the displays across campus.
examples.zh: 「交接资料包」里有已确认的图稿和校园各处展示点的地址。

examples.en: Our volunteers checked the handover package before giving the gallery keys to the next group.
examples.zh: 志愿者把画廊钥匙交给下一组之前，检查了「交接资料包」。

words.enDefinition: Detailed requirements for what the finished work should be like, such as size, format, or quality.

examples.en: The output specifications gave different dimensions for the lobby signs and the small table signs.
examples.zh: 「成品规格要求」为大堂标牌和桌面小牌给出了不同尺寸。

examples.en: Our team asked for the output specifications before editing the photographs for the exhibition wall.
examples.zh: 团队在为展墙修照片之前，请对方提供了「成品规格要求」。

words.enDefinition: To compare work with its original instructions to see whether the requirements are met.

examples.en: We stopped to check against the brief before sending the finished labels to the venue.
examples.zh: 把做好的标签送到场馆之前，我们先「对照任务说明核查」。

examples.en: The designer asked the volunteers to check against the brief while she counted the finished signs.
examples.zh: 设计员请志愿者「对照任务说明核查」，自己清点做好的标牌。

collocations: check the design against the brief
check against the brief before delivery

words.enDefinition: To correspond in relevant details to the sample that has already been agreed or accepted.

examples.en: The colour needed to match the approved sample before the gallery would accept the boards.
examples.zh: 颜色需要「与已确认的样品一致」，画廊才会接收这些展板。

examples.en: We checked whether the stand bases would match the approved sample after the material changed.
examples.zh: 材料改了之后，我们核查展架底座是否仍「与已确认的样品一致」。

collocations: match the approved sample in colour
make sure the items match the approved sample
check that the product will match the approved sample

words.enDefinition: To provide the promised work or materials in the way and at the time agreed.

examples.en: The student studio confirmed it could still deliver as agreed after replacing one of the materials.
examples.zh: 换了一种材料后，学生工作室确认仍可以「按约定交付」。

examples.en: We asked whether the team could deliver as agreed despite the change of venue on Friday.
examples.zh: 虽然周五换了场地，我们还是询问团队是否能「按约定交付」。

collocations: be ready to deliver as agreed
make sure we can deliver as agreed

words.enDefinition: Original project files that someone can open in the appropriate software and modify.

examples.en: The designer included editable source files so the club could update names for future events.
examples.zh: 设计员附上了「可编辑的源文件」，这样社团能为以后的活动更新名字。

examples.en: We asked for editable source files when the gallery wanted to translate the signs later.
examples.zh: 画廊打算日后翻译标牌时，我们请对方提供「可编辑的源文件」。

words.enDefinition: A person's or organisation's consent to use the artwork in the way discussed.

examples.en: The club asked for permission to use the artwork in the programme for next year's exhibition.
examples.zh: 社团询问能否取得「使用图稿的许可」，用在明年展览的手册里。

examples.en: We confirmed permission to use the artwork on the banner before placing the print order.
examples.zh: 我们先确认取得了「使用图稿的许可」，才下单印横幅。

collocations: ask for permission to use the artwork
receive permission to use the artwork
confirm permission to use the artwork

words.enDefinition: To finish passing the agreed work, materials, or information to the person taking over.

examples.en: The gallery needed to complete the handover before the student team left for its summer placements.
examples.zh: 画廊得在学生团队去参加暑期实习前「完成交接」。

examples.en: We used the meeting to complete the handover of designs and labels for the exhibition.
examples.zh: 我们利用这次会议「完成交接」，把展览设计稿和标签交了过去。

collocations: agree when to complete the handover

words.zhGloss: 验收有条件通过，须更正
words.enDefinition: A status saying that approval depends on making the specified corrections.
acceptedZhAnswers: 验收有条件通过，须更正

examples.en: The poster was marked “Accepted subject to corrections” because two sponsor names were still misspelled.
examples.zh: 还有两个赞助方的名字拼错了，所以海报被标为「验收有条件通过，须更正」。

examples.en: We read “Accepted subject to corrections” and checked which room numbers the organiser wanted changed.
examples.zh: 看到「验收有条件通过，须更正」后，我们确认了组织者想改哪些房间号。

collocations: mark something accepted subject to corrections
an outcome of accepted subject to corrections
list items as accepted subject to corrections

words.enDefinition: Requested changes that still need to be completed before work is ready.

examples.en: The designer shared a list of outstanding revisions before our group met at the studio.
examples.zh: 我们小组到工作室碰面前，设计员分享了一份「尚未完成的修改」清单。

examples.en: We finished the outstanding revisions after the venue confirmed the correct entrance for the event.
examples.zh: 场地方确认了活动的正确入口后，我们完成了「尚未完成的修改」。

words.enDefinition: A new version of a proof that reflects changes to an earlier preview.

examples.en: The printer sent a revised proof after we added the second speaker's name to the cover.
examples.zh: 我们把第二位讲者的名字加到封面后，印刷店发来了「修订后的校样」。

examples.en: The revised proof showed the new room number in the space beneath the small map.
examples.zh: 「修订后的校样」在小地图下方的位置显示了新房间号。

words.enDefinition: A message informing the client that the agreed work has been finished.

examples.en: Our organiser received a work completion notice before going to collect the new board covers.
examples.zh: 我们的组织者去领新展板封面之前，收到了「完工通知」。

examples.en: The studio sent a work completion notice to the gallery after finishing the printed labels.
examples.zh: 工场做完印制标签后，给画廊发了「完工通知」。

words.enDefinition: A document or entry showing what work was accepted, by whom, and on what date.

examples.en: The acceptance record named the student organiser who had approved the delivery of the finished signs.
examples.zh: 「验收记录」写明了是哪个学生组织者确认了成品标牌交付。

examples.en: We checked the acceptance record to confirm whether both sets of panels had been approved.
examples.zh: 我们查阅了「验收记录」，确认两套展板是否都已通过。

words.enDefinition: A review conducted before handing over agreed work or goods to catch remaining problems.

examples.en: We arranged a pre-delivery review to check the display labels before handing them to the gallery.
examples.zh: 我们安排了「交付前检查」，把展品标签交给画廊之前先核对一遍。

examples.en: The pre-delivery review revealed that one sponsor's name was missing from the rear banner.
examples.zh: 「交付前检查」发现后面的横幅漏掉了一家赞助方的名字。

words.enDefinition: To ask someone to fix a particular mistake in work they have already produced.

examples.en: We had to request a correction when one of the artist names was spelled incorrectly.
examples.zh: 有位艺术家的名字拼错了，我们只好「请求更正」。

examples.en: The gallery agreed we could request a correction before the studio printed the remaining copies.
examples.zh: 画廊同意，在工场印刷剩下的份数之前，我们可以「请求更正」。

collocations: request a correction to the text
request a correction to a name
ask how to request a correction
